evidence.curator_note: First alpha-cleavage (ring opening) of the stepwise retro-Diels-Alder of a 4-R-cyclohexene molecular ion. ARC COUNT: the book draws 3 arc(s) on the molecular ion (p.70) and all three are printed - this is a fully drawn 3-fishhook alpha-cleavage. Move <1> (top-right fishhook next to the dot) = the odd electron on the pi-ionized alkene carbon (map 6) into the forming C6=C7 pi bond; move <2> (large central arc across the top of the ring) = one electron of the breaking C2-C7 ring sigma bond into that same forming pi bond; move <3> (small top-left fishhook next to R) = the other electron of the C2-C7 bond onto the R-bearing carbon (map 2), its new radical site. LOCALIZATION (convention B/C): the alkene radical cation is drawn localized as C5(+)-C6(.), i.e. cation on map 5 (the '+' at the lower-right vertex) and the odd electron on map 6 (the dot at the upper-right vertex); the neutral C=C double bond of 4-R-cyclohexene sat between maps 5 and 6. Instantiated as R=C6H5 (4-phenylcyclohexene) so map 1 is the phenyl ipso carbon.

locator.section: 4 / Basic Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (retro-Diels-Alder, charge retention)

evidence.curator_note: Second alpha-cleavage on the ring-opened distonic radical cation gives the CHARGE-RETENTION products (eq 4.31): the allylic/benzylic radical (map 2) drives cleavage of the C3-C4 bond. ARC COUNT: the book draws 2 arc(s) - the two fishhooks printed on the left of the intermediate. Move <1> = odd electron (map 2) into the forming C2=C3 pi bond; move <2> = one C3-C4 sigma electron into that same pi bond. Move <3>, the other C3-C4 sigma electron onto map 4 (the new radical of the departing diene ion), is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page - the book simply prints the dot on the butadiene fragment). Charge stays on the C4-C7 diene fragment -> butadiene radical cation, m/z 54; the R-CH=CH2 alkene (styrene for R=C6H5) leaves neutral. PRINTED INTENSITIES for m/z 54: R=H 80% (relative to cyclohexene's C5H7+ base peak = 100%, IE 9.1); R=C6H5 0.4% (IE of the styrene fragment 8.4). This record instantiates R=C6H5, hence relative_intensity 0.004 - the low value reflects that phenyl diverts the charge to the migration channel (eq 4.32).

Cross-linked to MOD rules IMS_4_31_alpha1 (ring-opening first alpha cleavage) and IMS_4_31_alpha2 (second alpha cleavage, charge conservation). VERIFIED against their DFS. IMS_4_31_alpha1 '[C]1[C]2[C]3[C]4[C+]5[C.]6[C]7{-}2>>[C]1[C.]2[C]3[C]4[C+]5[C]6{=}[C]7' breaks the ring bond map2-map7, forms the C6=C7 pi bond and relocates the radical from map6 to map2 - exactly step_alpha1_ring_opening's bond changes (the rule map numbers align 1:1 with this record's map numbers). IMS_4_31_alpha2 '[C]1[C.]2[C]3[C]4[C+]5[C]6{=}[C]7>>[C]1[C]2{=}[C]3.[C.]4[C+]5[C]6{=}[C]7' cleaves map3-map4, forms C2=C3 and splits off the [C.]4[C+]5[C]6{=}[C]7 diene radical cation (charge retained) plus the neutral R-C2=C3 alkene - exactly step_alpha2_charge_retention. Both cleaved bonds are incident to the carbon that forms the new pi bond, so the rules are correctly encoded alpha-cleavages (no mismatch). The generic rules use a bare carbon at map1 as the R handle and require a substituent at map2, so they match this R=C6H5 substrate (map1 = phenyl ipso); they would NOT match plain cyclohexene (R=H) at map2, for which the generic ring cleavage IMS_4_30 is the relevant rule.
